sections.title: Overview
descriptions: This page brings together available employment and compensation records related to Steven G. Hawkins.
In the Ben Schneider (Reckless Ben) case, he made the March 9 vehicle stop, conducted sobriety tests, requested a police-dog sniff, and helped search the vehicle.

sections.title: Employment
descriptions: Officer Steven G. Hawkins began working for the American Fork Police Department on July 4, 2022.

segments.text: Officer Steven G. Hawkins was involved in the following police encounters:

contents.text_value: March 9, 2026: Hawkins spoke with Christian Morgan and issued a trespass warning, then stopped the vehicle associated with the visit. He conducted sobriety tests on Tyler Shaw, requested a police-dog sniff, and searched the vehicle with Fraughton. The report records a .000 breath-test result and release from the scene. See pages 6–9.

Hawkins wrote the March 9 narrative and acknowledged that his body-camera microphone was muted during part of the investigation. Attorney John Bryan’s review questions the length of the stop and highlights officers’ discussion of frightening the occupants and whether they had charges. These are concerns raised in Bryan’s analysis, rather than court findings.
